findings.title: TotalDocs ranges over the index cache without a lock while the watch goroutine can write to it
findings.body:
`TotalDocs` iterates `b.cache` without taking `cacheMu`. This PR adds a call to it in `searchSupport.init` (search.go:216), and that call happens after the event-handling goroutine has already started (search.go:207).

That goroutine runs `handleEvent` → `getOrCreateIndex` → `BuildIndex`, which writes `b.cache[key] = idx`. A write event for a resource not indexed at startup can therefore mutate the map while `TotalDocs` is iterating it. Go treats concurrent map iteration plus write as a fatal, unrecoverable runtime error, so the process crashes at startup.

Fix: take `b.cacheMu.RLock()` in `TotalDocs`, or compute the total before starting the watch goroutine.

findings.title: Narrowing the lock allows duplicate concurrent builds of the same index key
findings.body:
Previously `BuildIndex` held `cacheMu` for the whole build, and `GetIndex` (RLock) blocked until a build finished, so callers rarely built the same key twice. Now the lock covers only the final map assignment.

`getOrCreateIndex` does an unsynchronized check-then-build. Concurrent `Search` requests and `handleEvent` calls for a namespace not indexed at startup can therefore each run a full build for the same key. Consequences:
- Wasted work.
- `IndexTenants` and `IndexedKinds` metrics incremented multiple times.
- For file-based indexes, the second `bleve.New(dir, ...)` fails because the path already exists.
- The last build overwrites the cache entry, so documents that `handleEvent` wrote into an earlier, now-discarded index instance are lost.

A per-key lock or singleflight around build would give the speedup without these races.

findings.title: Stopped server no longer rejects requests
findings.body:
`Stop` sets `s.initErr` to "service is stopping" / "service is stopped". The only way that error reached callers was through the `s.Init(ctx)` check at the top of every gRPC handler, and this PR removes all of those checks.

After `Stop` cancels the server context and stops the backend, `Create`/`Update`/`Delete`/`Read`/`List`/`Watch`/`Search`/blob/health calls will still run against the stopped backend instead of failing fast with a clear error. `initErr` is now effectively dead state outside of `Init`.

Keep a cheap check of a stopped flag (ideally atomic) in the handlers, or remove the misleading `Stop` bookkeeping.

findings.title: Init failure in constructor leaks the context and background goroutines
findings.body:
When `s.Init(ctx)` fails, `NewResourceServer` returns `nil, err` without calling `cancel()`.

If `search.init` succeeded but a later step such as `initWatcher` failed, the search watch goroutine and the backend poller started by `WatchWriteEvents` keep running with no owner that can stop them. The search watch uses `context.Background()`.

Call `cancel()` on the error path. Ideally also tear down anything that `search.init` started.

findings.title: Integration test disabled for postgres instead of being fixed
findings.body:
The PR skips `TestIntegrationWillRunInstrumentationServerWhenTargetHasNoHttpServer` on postgres with the note "works locally". This PR changes startup behaviour: `NewResourceServer` now runs DB init, search index build and watcher setup synchronously.

The skip likely hides a regression or timing problem introduced by that change. For example, the test only sleeps 500ms before probing the HTTP server, and startup now blocks on indexing.

The postgres storage-server startup path loses CI coverage exactly when its behaviour changes.

findings.title: Data races on shared counters/err in parallel init workers
findings.body:
Inside the `errgroup` workers, two shared variables are written from multiple goroutines without synchronization:
- `totalBatchesIndexed++`
- `_, _, err = s.build(...)`, which writes the outer `err`

Before this PR the global `BuildIndex` lock serialized most of each worker's run. Now that the lock is removed so that builds run in parallel, these races are much more likely to be hit. The reported `namespaced_indexed` span attribute can be wrong, and the race detector will flag the code.

Use a local `err` in the closure and an `atomic.Int64` (or count after `Wait`).
